claims.claim: Confidentiality in healthcare means keeping a patient's health information private: OpenStax's Fundamentals of Nursing defines confidentiality as safeguarding health information so that it is not disclosed to unauthorized individuals.

Privacy in healthcare means a patient's information is kept confidential and shared only with individuals on a need-to-know basis; patients share sensitive personal information with healthcare workers to receive care, and workers are responsible for protecting it (ANA 2015, as cited by OpenStax FON 9.3).

HIPAA — the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act — is a U.S. federal law enacted in 1996 that protects the privacy and security of patients' health information; under HIPAA, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services issued the Privacy Rule establishing national standards for the protection of certain health information, with the Office for Civil Rights responsible for implementing and enforcing it.

The Privacy Rule applies to covered entities — health plans, health care clearinghouses, and any health care provider who transmits health information in electronic form in connection with standard transactions — as well as their business associates.

Protected health information (PHI) is individually identifiable health information held or transmitted by a covered entity in any form or media, whether electronic, paper, or oral; it includes common identifiers such as name, address, birth date, and Social Security number, and it relates to the individual's past, present, or future physical or mental health, the provision of health care, or payment for health care; OpenStax FON 9.3 adds demographic information, medical histories, test results, and health insurance information to the practical list.

The basic rule of the Privacy Rule: a covered entity may not use or disclose protected health information except as the Privacy Rule permits or requires, or as the individual who is the subject of the information authorizes in writing.

Permitted uses and disclosures without the individual's authorization include: to the individual; for treatment, payment, and health care operations; where the individual has the opportunity to agree or object; incidental to an otherwise permitted use; public interest and benefit activities; and limited data sets for research, public health, or health care operations.

Treatment is defined by HHS as the provision, coordination, or management of health care and related services for an individual by one or more health care providers, including consultation between providers regarding a patient and referral of a patient by one provider to another.

Public health exception: covered entities may disclose protected health information without authorization to public health authorities authorized by law to collect or receive such information for preventing or controlling disease, injury, or disability, and to authorities authorized to receive reports of child abuse and neglect; the permitted disclosures also cover FDA-regulated products (adverse event reporting, recalls) and, where authorized by law, notification of individuals who may have been exposed to a communicable disease.

The minimum necessary standard: a covered entity must make reasonable efforts to use, disclose, and request only the minimum amount of protected health information needed to accomplish the intended purpose; OpenStax FON 9.3 states the standard requires healthcare workers to only access and disclose the minimum amount of PHI necessary to perform their job duties.

Patients' rights under the Privacy Rule: patients may access their protected health information, request corrections to it, and receive an accounting of disclosures; OpenStax FON 9.3 states HIPAA gives patients the right to access their PHI, request corrections, and receive an accounting of disclosures.

Everyday privacy practice in nursing: nurses protect patient information by logging in with a password, logging off after each interaction, ensuring no unauthorized person is viewing the computer screen, and taking care when having conversations in which patient information may be shared.

Hospitalized patients have a right to privacy when their information is discussed between healthcare workers and to confidentiality of communications and records; OpenStax FON 16.3 gives the example of discussing a patient, including their name and medical information, in an elevator containing people without a reason to know the information as a breach of privacy and confidentiality.

HIPAA is a privacy floor, not a total barrier: HHS states the Privacy Rule's major goal is to assure that individuals' health information is properly protected while allowing the flow of health information needed to provide and promote high-quality health care and to protect the public's health — a balance that permits important uses while protecting the privacy of people who seek care.

conflictingEvidence.issue: 'Confidentiality means never sharing any health information with anyone' — a common over-reading of HIPAA.
positions: The Privacy Rule's basic principle is that a covered entity may not use or disclose PHI except as the Rule permits or requires, or as the individual authorizes in writing (HHS OCR).

The Rule explicitly permits disclosure without authorization for defined purposes: to the individual, treatment, payment, health care operations, opportunity to agree or object, public interest and benefit activities (including public health), and limited data sets (HHS OCR).
Confidentiality therefore means protecting information from unauthorized disclosure while allowing the necessary flow of information for care and public health — not secrecy from everyone, always.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson states the exceptions factually (treatment, payment, patient request, public health) and frames confidentiality as protection from unauthorized disclosure, citing the OCR summary's own framing of the Rule as a balance.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Privacy, confidentiality, and security are often used interchangeably.
positions: OpenStax FON 9.3 defines them separately: confidentiality is safeguarding information from disclosure to unauthorized individuals; privacy means information is kept confidential and shared only on a need-to-know basis; security is the technical and administrative protection (passwords, firewalls, encryption) of the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic health information.
In everyday speech the terms blur, but the distinctions matter for practice and for the law.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson defines privacy and confidentiality from OpenStax FON 9.3 and contrasts confidentiality with security in the Compare / Contrast section.
